messages:
Caroline (oncall): alert from monitoring — sustained GPU allocation failures in asia-southeast1 for the last 4m, API 503 rate up 22% :red_circle:
infra-bot: metric snapshot: region=asia-southeast1, gpu_alloc_errors=214, host_p95_latency=780ms, free_gpu_count=0, pending_provision=47
Sam (infra): I see autoscale attempted 3x, all provisioning requests returned quota_exhausted from cloud provider
Raj (sre): confirm: is this a provider capacity issue or our quota config?
Sam (infra): cloud returned "insufficient capacity in region" on new instance requests — looks like region-level exhaustion, not our IAM quota
Maya (prodops): customers seeing 503s? range? any high-SLA tenants impacted?
Caroline (oncall): yes — top 10 customers degraded. Early users on dedicated pools hitting rate limits. Incident severity P1. Opening incident in PagerDuty now.
Nate (eng): proposing immediate traffic shift for non-dedicated traffic to fallback regions (us-west1, europe-west1). Need checklist for safe shift (model variants, latency, KV cache invalidation)
Raj (sre): agree. Steps: 1) mark asia-southeast1 as degraded in routing policy 2) enable allow-fallback=true for low-priority routes 3) throttle bursty jobs
Sam (infra): command to flip policy (one-liner):
```
redwoodctl routing update --policy "prio: asia-southeast1=0,us-west1=1,europe-west1=2" --force-canary 100
```
Sam (infra): can run now but expect higher latency for APAC users; we can do partial canary to 50% first
Caroline (oncall): start canary 10% then observe 5m, roll to 50% if errors <1%
Maya (prodops): also disable non-critical background jobs (batch embedding backfills). Those are scheduled on shared pools and can be evicted.
Nate (eng): evict command: `kubectl label nodes --selector=pool=shared app=backfill eviction=true` — will reduce pressure on schedulers
Support-Bot: created ticket INC-2026-193 in incidents board, notified growth and sales
Raj (sre): can someone open a cloud provider support case? We need capacity info and ETA for extra GPUs in region
Sam (infra): on it — support case #CS-75921 created, attaching logs and cluster trace. Provider replied initial ETA unknown, they're investigating
Caroline (oncall): good. Also need temporary mitigations: 1) route heavy token-generation models to quantized variants 2) reduce max_tokens defaults to 512 for affected routes via runtime override
Nate (eng): we have quantized variants available for gpt-style models. Quick config:
```
POST /v1/configs/overrides
{ "match": "routes:/generate", "overrides": {"model_variant": "gpt-q4", "max_tokens": 512} }
```
Maya (prodops): schedule: canary traffic shift started at +0:10, metrics: request_errors 503 -> 12% -> target <1%
Raj (sre): also add temporary capacity tag to Dedicated pools to accept burst from Hosted where contracts allow. Need finance ok?
Caroline (oncall): finance notified, they approved temporary burst for up to 48h under emergency fund :white_check_mark:
Sam (infra): rolling policy update now (canary 10%). Watching logs.
infra-bot: routing change applied: canary=10% -> backend=us-west1,europe-west1. Observability: errors trending down to 7%
Caroline (oncall): good. Set slack alerts to 5m cadence for api_errors and host_latency. Notify customers via status page.
Maya (prodops): status page update drafted and published — "Degraded performance in APAC region; mitigation in progress; non-critical background tasks paused"
Nate (eng): quick sanity: KV cache invalidation risk — note that prefix caching won't be available for shifted traffic; add a note to rollout: "expect transient cold starts for shifted sessions"
Raj (sre): action items assigned: Sam -> follow cloud case and escalate, Nate -> apply model_variant overrides, Maya -> customer comms + pause backfills, Caroline -> monitor + runbook owner
Caroline (oncall): tagging execs and legal as well. Estimated remediation: provider dependent. If provider cannot supply capacity in 2h, plan full failover for critical traffic to europe/us and discuss temporary regional SLAs
Sam (infra): cloud provider responded: "best-effort allocation underway; no firm ETA" — escalated to account manager
Caroline (oncall): OK. Continue shift to 50% if errors continue to drop. Keep incident channel updated every 15m.
Maya (prodops): FYI — projected incremental cost if we fully shift 100% to fallback regions + burst capacity ~ +$18k/day (estimate)
Raj (sre): noted. We'll run cost vs. SLA tradeoff if this goes >4h
Caroline (oncall): thanks team. Next update in 15. If anyone finds customer-impacting errors, ping PD immediately. :rocket:
